cases.input: The printer only prints blank white pages

runs.answer:
Based on **“Printer output is empty or faded”**:

1. Open the printer’s front panel. Check that the toner cartridge is seated firmly and, if it’s new, that the orange protective strip has been removed.
2. Print a configuration page from the printer menu.
3. If the configuration page is blank too, the printer needs a new cartridge; facilities can supply one. If it prints normally, reinstall the printer from the self service portal.

results.title: Printer output is empty or faded
results.content: When a network printer feeds paper but the sheets come out without any print, the cause is almost always the toner. Print a configuration page from the printer menu: if that page is also empty, the device needs a new cartridge, which facilities can supply. If the configuration page looks fine, the problem is in the document or driver, so reinstall the printer from the self service portal.

cases.input: Nobody can hear me in Teams meetings

runs.answer:
In the Teams meeting, open **Device settings** and confirm the correct microphone is selected. If you’re using a headset, check its physical mute switch; if it’s connected through a docking station, connect it directly to your laptop. Then use Teams’ **Test call** to check the microphone.

Based on **“Sound and microphone problems in Teams calls.”**

args.query: Nobody can hear me in Microsoft Teams meetings microphone audio troubleshooting

results.title: Sound and microphone problems in Teams calls
results.content: If other participants cannot hear you, or you cannot hear them, first open the device settings in Teams during the call and confirm that the correct speaker and microphone are selected. Headsets connected through a docking station are sometimes not picked up, so try connecting them directly to the laptop. Check that the microphone is not muted by a physical switch on the headset. Use the test call function in the settings to record and play back a short message. Bluetooth headsets should be paired again if the audio is choppy or keeps dropping out.

judge.reasoning: The answer names the knowledge-base article and includes all four relevant steps: select the correct microphone, check the headset mute switch, bypass the dock, and use a test call. It stays grounded in the article and is concise.

cases.input: Hi! Since this morning my laptop has been really slow

runs.answer:
Try these steps:

- Restart your laptop to finish any pending updates.
- In Task Manager, check which apps are using the most memory and close ones you don’t need.
- Free up disk space, aiming to keep at least 20% available. Remove old downloads and empty the recycle bin.
- Close browser tabs you aren’t using.

If it’s still slow after that, it may need a hardware check by the service desk.

Based on **“Improving laptop responsiveness.”**

args.query: Laptop running very slow performance troubleshooting since this morning

results.title: Improving laptop responsiveness
results.content: Computers become sluggish over time when they are rarely restarted, when disk space runs low or when many applications run at once. Restart the laptop at least once a week, because updates are only finished during a restart. Open Task Manager to see which applications use the most memory and close the ones you do not need. Keep at least 20 percent of the disk free by removing old downloads and emptying the recycle bin. Browser tabs use a lot of memory as well. If the device is still slow after these steps, it may need a hardware check by the service desk.

judge.reasoning: The answer names the knowledge-base article and gives all requested steps: restart, close memory-heavy apps and tabs, and free disk space. Its additional details and service-desk suggestion are grounded in the article.
